subject: Inference deployment route & pricing decision checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@avatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + pricing assumptions we discussed

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap to make sure we're aligned and to flag the items we need from your side before the technical deep-dive:

Summary of needs from AvaTech
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency for customer-facing recommendations (p95 target ~350ms) while keeping unit cost predictable for enterprise billing.
- Data residency: must remain in US-only cloud regions; potential requirement to run in customer VPC for Prod.
- Usage profile (from your note): 300M tokens/month initially, ramp to ~1B tokens/month over 12 months.

Options discussed (high level)
1) Hosted API (Redwood) — fastest to ship, per-token billing, no infra ops for AvaTech. Good for low friction pilots.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — reserved GPU pools with monthly commits, better unit economics at scale and predictable spend.
3) Private VPC / on-prem — highest control for data residency/compliance; requires customer infra or cloud marketplace deployment and an MSA for private deployments.

Initial cost-back-of-envelope (ballpark; we'll refine with exact model/filters in the deep-dive):
- Hosted: $0.0009 per generated token (assumes standard medium-sized gen model we tested). At 300M tokens -> ~$270k/mo. At 1B tokens -> ~$900k/mo.
- Dedicated (reserved): baseline reserved pool $30k/mo (covers baseline throughput and platform fees) + incremental infra amortization. At 1B tokens effective unit ~ $0.00032/token (assuming 1 reserved pool + autoscale burst policy).
- Private VPC: Redwood license + infra. Example: license $40k/mo + infra costs. If AvaTech supplies infra and achieves 1B tokens, unit cost could fall ~ $0.00020 - $0.00030/token but with upfront ops work and OPEX variability depending on instance choice.

Questions / items we need from AvaTech before pricing firm-up
- Confirmation of token definition (do you count input+output tokens or only outputs for billing?)
- Expected concurrency (RPS) and p95 latency SLA expectations during peak windows
- Any minimum security controls (KMS/HSM, SOC2 evidence) beyond the standard questionnaire attached

Attached: Pilot_SOW_v1.docx (baseline pilot scope) and an outline for a quick-cost model.

Proposed next steps
- Sarah: confirm token definition and share concurrency targets + any procurement timing constraints.
- Redwood: schedule a technical deep-dive (45–60 min) with infra/ops & ML engineers to validate throughput assumptions and finalize a pricing scenario.

If that summary looks right, I'll send over 2 concrete pricing scenarios (hosted vs reserved) with line-item assumptions before the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear summary, Karthik. That aligns with our discussion. A few clarifications: 

- Token definition: for internal billing we count input + output tokens. Please model both.
- Concurrency: peak is ~120 requests per second (avg request ~1.2k tokens total). p95 latency target 350ms, p99 < 750ms.
- Security: we completed high-level SOC2 screening, but we will need proof of data isolation for Prod (VPC option preferred). I attached a terse security checklist — can you confirm which items Redwood covers in hosted vs dedicated vs private?
- Procurement timeline: target pilot sign-off by end of August; procurement expects a 30–60 day review window after receiving SOW and pricing.

Given the need for predictability, procurement will want to see a reserved option with a committed monthly cap and a clear overage policy. 

I'll review the attached SOW and return marked comments by EoD tomorrow.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@avatech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap + pricing assumptions we discussed — proposed scenarios

Hi Sarah — looping in the engineering cost model and a clean comparison so procurement has something concrete. Below are two scenarios with assumptions called out. These are still draft numbers; we can lock after the technical deep-dive.

Assumptions (apply to both scenarios)
- Token = input + output; monthly tokens: Month0 = 300M, Month12 = 1B
- Model profile: mid-size generation model; p95 latency target assumes Redwood-optimized kernels + continuous batching
- Storage/retention and audit logs billed separately; not included in per-token numbers below

Scenario A — Hosted (fastest path)
- Price: $0.00085 per token (volume tiering starts at 500M tokens -> discounted to $0.00072/token)
- Cost example: Month0 (300M) -> $255,000/mo. Month12 (1B w/ tiering) -> ~$800k/mo
- Pros: no infra ownership, rapid pilot; SOC2 evidence available; Data residency via region restriction (US) but not VPC-isolated.
- Cons: higher per-token at scale; limited customer-managed networking.

Scenario B — Dedicated reserved capacity
- Structure: monthly commitment + variable per-token overage. Example commit: $28,000/month reserved pool covering baseline capacity; commit sized to meet steady throughput for ~300–500M tokens.
- Overcommit pricing: additional tokens billed at $0.00030/token up to 1B; effective blended rate at 1B (with a reasonable commit) ~ $0.00034/token.
- Example math (1B tokens): commit $28k + overage (700M * $0.00030) = $28k + $210k = $238k -> effective $0.000238/token.
- Pros: predictable monthly bill, better unit economics, can support VPC peering for stronger network isolation.
- Cons: longer lead time to provision larger reserved pools; commit required.

Scenario C — Private (VPC / on-prem) — high-control option
- Structure: Redwood private license $40k/mo + customer infra. Example infra cost (customer-managed): $0.00018/token at 1B tokens (depending on instance selection and utilization).
- Pros: full data isolation, customer-managed keys, lowest unit cost at very high utilization.
- Cons: ops responsibility on AvaTech, multi-week setup for on-prem or marketplace deployment, support/managed services add-on if desired.

Procurement-friendly pricing elements we can include
- Clear commit tiers (e.g., 0–500M, 500M–1B) with breakpoint discounts
- Overage caps and predictable escalation (e.g., 20% overage cap for first 3 months)
- A short-term pilot SKU (60-day) on hosted with conversion credits if you commit to Dedicated within 90 days

Next steps we propose
1) Technical deep-dive (45–60 min) — scope: concurrency validation, latency profiling, networking requirements for VPC peering. Owners: Ben (infra), Marissa (solutions).
2) Redwood to share a line-item quote for the two most likely paths (Hosted pilot vs Dedicated commit) within 48 hours of deep-dive.
3) Procurement: please send any SOW redlines and preferred procurement cadence so we can align contract templates early.

I can prepare a one-page pricing brief with the numbers above and a simple sensitivity table (tokens vs effective unit price). If that helps procurement, say the word and I’ll attach it to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — we’ll wait on Sarah's security answers before finalizing the VPC wording.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
